_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Panama covering Cuna/Kuna/Guna indigenous peoples, isthmus strategic importance, Balboa 1513 (first European to see Pacific from Americas), colonial transit route (gold/silver, Porto Bello fairs), pirate attacks (Henry Morgan 1671), Gran Colombia, separation from Colombia 1903 (US-orchestrated, Philippe Bunau-Varilla), Panama Canal 1904-14 (US built after French failure/De Lesseps), Canal Zone (US sovereignty), Torrijos-Carter Treaties 1977 (returned canal), Noriega CIA-to-prisoner, US invasion 1989, canal handover 1999, and global shipping hub.

country_profile.currency: Panamanian balboa (PAB, pegged 1:1 to USD); US dollar (USD) in circulation

religion.note: Catholic dominant; evangelical growth; Afro-Caribbean Protestant communities; small Hindu (Indian), Jewish, Bahá'í, Muslim; indigenous spiritual practices

ethnic_groups.name: Mestizo
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Indigenous-European; dominant identity; culturally Spanish-speaking

ethnic_groups.name: Afro-Panamanian
ethnic_groups.notes: Colonial-era Black (Colon, Panama City) plus West Indian (Barbadian/Jamaican, Canal workers); English-speaking; significant cultural/demographic group

ethnic_groups.name: White
ethnic_groups.notes: Spanish descent; also European immigrants; elite Panamanian families (rabiblancos)

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous
ethnic_groups.notes: Guna/Kuna (San Blas/Guna Yala islands, molas, autonomous comarca), Ngäbe-Buglé (largest, western mountains), Emberá, Wounaan, Naso/Teribe, Bri Bri; land rights autonomy

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese/Asian
ethnic_groups.notes: Cantonese Chinese (arrived for railroad/canal, 19th century); significant in retail; also Indian (Hindu), Korean, Japanese

country_profile.notes_unique: Panama Canal (opened 1914, connects Atlantic/Pacific, world's most strategic waterway, ~14,000 ships/year); born from US conspiracy (Philippe Bunau-Varilla, 1903 secession from Colombia); Canal Zone (US sovereign territory 1903-79); Torrijos-Carter Treaties 1977 (canal returned 1999); Manuel Noriega (CIA asset turned enemy, indicted for drug trafficking, US invasion 1989, 23 years imprisoned); international banking/finance hub; dollarized economy; flag of convenience (world's largest ship registry); Guna Yala (autonomous indigenous comarca); Balboa 1513 (first European at Pacific); Darien Gap (jungle, no road); Panama Papers 2016 (Mossack Fonseca, global tax evasion scandal)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: José Raúl Mulino
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: RM party; former security minister under Martinelli; ran as stand-in after Martinelli barred; anti-corruption mandate; businessman; tackling migration (Darien Gap)

former_leaders.name: Laurentino Cortizo
former_leaders.notes: PRD; businessman; COVID pandemic; Darien migration crisis; leukemia diagnosis

former_leaders.name: Juan Carlos Varela
former_leaders.notes: PP; VP who broke with Martinelli; ended Taiwan recognition (switched to China); Panama Papers scandal

former_leaders.name: Ricardo Martinelli
former_leaders.notes: Supermarket tycoon; populist; infrastructure; wiretapping scandal; convicted (fled to US, extradited, imprisoned); barred from presidency

former_leaders.name: Martín Torrijos
former_leaders.notes: PRD; son of Omar Torrijos; canal expansion referendum 2006 (approved); social programs

former_leaders.name: Mireya Moscoso
former_leaders.notes: First female president; Arnúlfista; widow of Arnulfo Arias; canal handover December 31, 1999; corruption allegations

former_leaders.name: Ernesto Pérez Balladares
former_leaders.notes: PRD; banker; referendum to seek re-election (rejected); post-Noriega reconstruction

former_leaders.name: Manuel Noriega
former_leaders.notes: Military dictator; 'Maximum Leader'; G-2 intelligence chief; CIA asset (recruited by George H.W. Bush); drug trafficking; indicted by US; resisted; US invasion Dec 1989 (Operation Just Cause, Vatican embassy refuge); 40 years US prison; died 2017

former_leaders.name: Omar Torrijos
former_leaders.notes: Military strongman; populist; negotiated Torrijos-Carter Treaties 1977 (canal return); national hero; died plane crash 1981 (conspiracy theories); Noriega succeeded him

910.name: Pre-Columbian Panama
910.description: Early habitation on the isthmus, Coclé gold-working traditions, Barriles chiefdoms, Chibchan peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Early Isthmus Habitation
sub_clusters.description: Paleo-Indian through Archaic settlement, early cultivation in tropical forest, Lake Alajuela sites.

sub_clusters.name: Coclé Gold-Working Tradition
sub_clusters.description: Sitio Conte and El Caño burial sites, spectacular gold huacas (figurines), polychrome pottery.

sub_clusters.name: Barriles Chiefdoms
sub_clusters.description: Highland Chiriquí chiefdoms, volcanic-stone statuary of warriors riding captives, hierarchical society.

920.name: Isthmus Chiefdoms and Trade Networks
920.description: Complex chiefdoms linking Mesoamerican and South American trade zones, Cuna/Guna, Ngäbe-Buglé, Emberá peoples.

sub_clusters.name: El Caño and Late Coclé Chiefdoms
sub_clusters.description: Elaborate tombs, golden breastplates, agate beads, ceremonial centre near Natá.

sub_clusters.name: Guna, Ngäbe-Buglé, and Emberá Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Indigenous nations of the isthmus at contact: Guna on Caribbean coast, Ngäbe-Buglé in western highlands, Emberá in Darién.

sub_clusters.name: Darién Trade Hub
sub_clusters.description: Isthmus as biological and cultural corridor, gold and shell trade between Colombia and Mesoamerica.

930.name: Spanish Conquest and Transit Colony
930.description: Balboa's Pacific discovery, colonial transit route (Camino de Cruces), Portobelo fairs, pirate raids.

sub_clusters.name: Balboa and the Discovery of the Pacific
sub_clusters.description: Vasco Núñez de Balboa crosses the Darién, first European to sight the Pacific Ocean from the Americas.

sub_clusters.name: Panamá Viejo and Colonial Transit
sub_clusters.description: Oldest European city on the Pacific coast, Camino de Cruces, Peruvian silver transit, burned by Morgan.

sub_clusters.name: Portobelo Trade Fairs
sub_clusters.description: Massive treasure fairs linking Spain and South America, fortifications, Drake's death, British attacks.

sub_clusters.name: Scottish Darién Scheme
sub_clusters.description: Scotland's failed colonial venture at Caledonia Bay, contributing to the 1707 Act of Union with England.

940.name: Panama as Colombian Province
940.description: Independence from Spain, union with Gran Colombia then New Granada/Colombia, Panama Railroad, separatist attempts.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Union with Colombia
sub_clusters.description: Independence from Spain (28 Nov 1821), voluntary union with Bolívar's Gran Colombia, federal tensions.

sub_clusters.name: Panama Railroad (1855)
sub_clusters.description: First transcontinental railroad in the Americas, California Gold Rush transit, Chinese and Caribbean labour, transformative.

sub_clusters.name: French Canal Attempt (De Lesseps)
sub_clusters.description: Ferdinand de Lesseps's sea-level canal attempt, 20,000+ worker deaths (malaria/yellow fever), bankruptcy scandal.

940.name: Panamanian Independence (1903)
940.description: US-backed separation from Colombia, Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty, Canal Zone sovereignty surrendered.

sub_clusters.name: Separation from Colombia
sub_clusters.description: US warships prevent Colombian intervention, Philippe Bunau-Varilla negotiates treaty without Panamanians present.

sub_clusters.name: Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty
sub_clusters.description: US gains perpetual sovereignty over 10-mile Canal Zone, annual payment, source of lasting resentment.

950.name: Panama Canal Construction
950.description: American construction of the Panama Canal: lock system, Culebra Cut, malaria eradication, Afro-Caribbean labour.

sub_clusters.name: Canal Engineering and Construction
sub_clusters.description: Lock-based design (Goethals), Culebra Cut, Gatun Dam, 75,000 workers, 5,600+ deaths.

sub_clusters.name: Gorgas and Disease Eradication
sub_clusters.description: William Gorgas's anti-mosquito campaign conquers yellow fever and malaria, enabling canal completion.

sub_clusters.name: West Indian Canal Workers
sub_clusters.description: Afro-Caribbean workers from Barbados, Jamaica, Trinidad — Silver Roll segregation, lasting Panamanian community.

950.name: Canal Zone Era
950.description: US-governed Canal Zone as a 'state within a state', sovereignty protests, 1964 Martyrs' Day, Torrijos-Carter treaty.

sub_clusters.name: Canal Zone Enclave
sub_clusters.description: American-administered zone, Zonians community, Jim Crow–style segregation, Panamanian resentment.

sub_clusters.name: Martyrs' Day (9 January 1964)
sub_clusters.description: Panamanian students demand right to fly flag in Canal Zone, US military kills 22, diplomatic break.

sub_clusters.name: Torrijos-Carter Treaties (1977)
sub_clusters.description: Omar Torrijos negotiates canal handover, phased transfer, neutrality guarantee, achieved national aspiration.

960.name: Noriega and US Invasion
960.description: Manuel Noriega's dictatorship, drug trafficking, stolen election, US invasion (Operation Just Cause).

sub_clusters.name: Noriega Dictatorship
sub_clusters.description: Military strongman, CIA asset turned adversary, drug trafficking, Spadafora murder, 1989 election annulled.

sub_clusters.name: US Invasion — Operation Just Cause
sub_clusters.description: 26,000 US troops invade (20 Dec 1989), Noriega surrenders, hundreds-thousands of Panamanian casualties.

960.name: Canal Handover and Expansion
960.description: Historic canal transfer to Panama (31 Dec 1999), referendum, expanded locks opened 2016.

sub_clusters.name: Canal Transfer (31 December 1999)
sub_clusters.description: Panama assumes full control of the canal, Mireya Moscoso receives canal, sovereignty fulfilled.

sub_clusters.name: Canal Expansion (Third Set of Locks)
sub_clusters.description: 2006 referendum approves $5.25B expansion, new Neopanamax locks open June 2016, doubling capacity.

960.name: Contemporary Panama
960.description: Banking centre, Panama Papers, Cobre Panamá mine protests, canal drought crisis, democratic stability.

sub_clusters.name: Banking and Financial Centre
sub_clusters.description: Offshore banking hub, dollarised economy, Colón Free Trade Zone, income inequality despite growth.

sub_clusters.name: Panama Papers Scandal
sub_clusters.description: Mossack Fonseca leak reveals global offshore network, 11.5 million documents, reputational damage.

sub_clusters.name: Cobre Panamá Mine Protests
sub_clusters.description: Massive protests against copper mining contract, Supreme Court rules unconstitutional, mine closure.

sub_clusters.name: Canal Drought Crisis
sub_clusters.description: El Niño drought reduces canal transits, global trade impact, climate vulnerability of canal operations.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
